resources.string: Retrobit uses this service to detect focused text fields, insert dictation directly, and read volume buttons when a trigger is enabled. With screen-context opt-in, a snapshot is captured when an assistant session starts and is sent to your selected LLM only if your command asks to read or reply to screen content; it is not stored in history.
Dictate at the speed of speech, plus an assistant that understands real commands — all in one app.
Tap the button and speak. The result shows up here.
Three minutes once, then everything runs automatically.
The best way to dictate in any app.

Voice commands, questions, and app control — offline first, online AI when enabled.
Examples: \"open WhatsApp\", \"call Mom\", \"set alarm 5 am\", \"timer 10 minutes\", \"turn on flashlight\", \"note pay the bill\", \"search for rendang recipe\".
The message has not been sent. Approve to open a draft in the messaging app; review it and tap Send.
Hybrid: try on-device first, cloud as a fallback.
API keys are stored encrypted on device (Android Keystore) and sent only to the provider you choose.
Text is inserted directly at the cursor. If no text field is focused or no direct route is available, Retrobit does not use the clipboard automatically.
Requires the accessibility service to be on.
Ready. Hold a volume button to record, release to finish — the volume stays unchanged.
Ready. Press once to start/stop — the volume still changes as usual.
Turn on the Retrobit accessibility service first so the volume buttons can be read.
Hold Volume Up for the assistant; Volume Down remains the dictation trigger.
Hold Volume Up for the assistant
Requires accessibility. When enabled, Volume Up is reserved for the assistant: hold it for about 0.7 seconds to open a session. Volume Down still adjusts volume, or triggers dictation if enabled.
Ready. Volume Up is now an assistant shortcut (not a volume control); hold for about 0.7 seconds. Volume Down still adjusts volume or triggers dictation.
Ready. Hold Volume Up for the assistant; Volume Down remains the dictation trigger.
Even without online AI, dozens of commands work through local rules.

Off by default. When enabled, a snapshot is captured as an assistant session starts, but sent to your selected LLM only if your command asks to read or reply to screen content; it is not saved in history.
Enable the accessibility service to read a screen snapshot on request. Passwords and text being edited are excluded.

Opt-in is on: one snapshot is captured when an assistant session starts and forwarded to your selected LLM only for screen-related requests. Passwords/editable fields are excluded; it is not saved in history.

With Retrobit accessibility or keyboard active, a focused non-password text field routes the wake word to dictation; outside typing mode, the assistant listens for a command. Continuous listening costs extra battery.
Panel turns bright, like an e-reader in sunlight.
Appears only when a text field is focused. Tap for hands-free dictation; long-press for the assistant.
The JSON file holds your API keys in plain text — keep it somewhere safe. Useful for restoring settings after the app is uninstalled, because the storage key is wiped too.
No log yet. Run a dictation once to see activity.
Follow these five steps. Afterwards you can dictate and summon the assistant from any app.
Open the keyboard picker and choose \"Retrobit Voice\". You can switch back anytime with the keyboard button in the Retrobit bar.

Find \"Retrobit Voice — direct insertion\" in the installed services list and enable it. It detects focused fields and inserts dictation directly; screen reading stays off until you opt in under Settings.
Enable \"Display over other apps\". The bubble is visible only while a text field is focused.
Then a long-press of Home opens Retrobit and starts listening.
Disable battery optimization for Retrobit so recording and the wake word survive screen-off.
Recording is capped (3 minutes max) and stops when you go quiet.
On-device mode works with no internet at all — great for private notes.
Audio is deleted right after transcription when you use an on-device engine.
Online assistant features activate only with your own API key.
Screen context is off by default; a snapshot is read only after opt-in and your request, and is not saved in history.
Shown while the microphone is used for dictation.
Bubble appears only at a focused text field; tap to dictate, long-press for the assistant.
Grant \"Display over other apps\" to use the bubble.
